question.problem:
Given that $3a≡3b\,(\text{mod}\,12),$ which of the following statements **must** be true?

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,3)$
- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,4)$
- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,6)$
question.worked_solution:
The division property of modular arithmetic states that for $k\ne 0,$ we have

$$
ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)\,⟺\,a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

We're asked to consider the following statement:

$$
3a≡3b\,(\text{mod}\,12)
$$

Notice that $\text{gcd}(3,12)=3.$

Applying the division property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}3a & ≡3b &  & (\text{mod}\,12) \\ 3\cdot a & ≡3\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,3\cdot 4) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot a & ≡\cancel{3}\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{3}\cdot 4) \\ a & ≡b &  & (\text{mod}\,4)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".
